task: Repair the existing Template Factory quality catalog so compiler-owned provenance and showroomEvidence reach the quality acceptance proof and Product Owner handoff readiness path without duplicating authority.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The Template Factory compiler already emits exact candidate provenance and showroomEvidence, but the visual-fidelity quality catalog drops both fields before the quality gate builds acceptanceProofs. The downstream Product Owner handoff therefore sees factoryIdentityPinned=false and showroomContractPassed=false and can skip a candidate that is otherwise compiler-ready and browser-matrix-ready.
observableOutcomes: Every factory candidate catalog record carries the exact compiler report provenance object unchanged.
Every factory candidate catalog record carries the exact compiler report showroomEvidence rows unchanged.
The existing quality gate derives factoryIdentityPinned=true and showroomContractPassed=true from those propagated fields when the compiler data is valid.
The existing Product Owner target resolver becomes reachable from real acceptanceProofs without weakening any readiness condition.
unresolvedRisks: The catalog could reconstruct provenance instead of forwarding compiler authority, creating a second identity source.
Showroom evidence could be partially copied and silently lose reachability/navigation fields required by the handoff verifier.
A test could prove source text only while the GET payload still omits or mutates the fields.

in: Factory candidate quality catalog serialization boundary.
Adversarial regression of the catalog GET payload and downstream-ready field shape.
out: Product Owner browser journey behavior itself.
Template Factory golden visual diff sensitivity.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This path gates Product Owner acceptance and previously produced a material false-negative by dropping already-proven evidence. The repair is intentionally narrow: preserve a single authority, prove exact payload identity, and exercise the real catalog response without redesigning handoff or compiler behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: Factory candidate catalog provenance deep-equals build.report.provenance for the same recipe.
Factory candidate catalog showroomEvidence deep-equals build.report.showroomEvidence for the same recipe.
No synthetic fallback provenance/showroom evidence is created in the catalog.
The downstream quality gate and Product Owner handoff continue consuming the existing acceptanceProof fields without new parallel contracts.
invariants: Template Factory compiler report remains the sole provenance/showroom evidence owner.
Catalog serialization may copy values but may not recompute candidate identity.
Non-factory accepted templates and quality candidates retain their current payload shape and behavior.
A compiler-not-ready candidate remains excluded exactly as before.

failureModes: Catalog omits both fields and handoff target remains unreachable.
Catalog forwards provenance but not showroom evidence.
Catalog copies only partial showroom rows and navigation completeness later fails.
Catalog invents identity from recipe values instead of retaining compiler authority.
edgeCases: Factory recipe is productOwnerReady=false and therefore must remain absent.
Showroom evidence contains multiple page types and shell-navigation reachability rows.
Compiler provenance contains foundation template identity distinct from target template.
VISUAL_FIDELITY_QA is disabled and route must still return 404.

alternatives.summary: Forward provenance and showroomEvidence directly from build.report into the factory candidate catalog record.
alternatives.reason: This repairs the broken dataflow while preserving one canonical compiler-owned evidence authority.

alternatives.summary: Reconstruct provenance and showroom evidence inside the visual-fidelity API from recipe and package data.
alternatives.reason: That would create a second evidence authority and allow compiler/catalog identities to drift.

alternatives.summary: Remove factoryIdentityPinned or showroomContractPassed from Product Owner target readiness.
alternatives.reason: That would hide the evidence-loss defect and weaken a previously valid fail-closed acceptance requirement.

specialistReviews.finding: The compiler already owns the complete evidence; the defect is a serialization boundary that drops it.
specialistReviews.resolution: Forward compiler fields unchanged rather than introducing another builder or handoff authority.

specialistReviews.finding: Quality acceptance already consumes manifest.provenance and manifest.showroomEvidence correctly when present.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep scripts/template-factory-quality-gate.mjs unchanged and restore its expected inputs.

specialistReviews.finding: A green compiler/browser path is insufficient if final handoff evidence does not bind candidate identity and showroom navigation.
specialistReviews.resolution: Regression-test the real GET payload and retain existing downstream readiness predicates unchanged.

specialistReviews.finding: TF-KF-005 already describes green technical proof failing to bind the Product Owner path to the same candidate identity.
specialistReviews.resolution: Repair the existing contract path and keep the procedural-memory rule active.

challenge.finding: factoryIdentityPinned can recover while showroomContractPassed remains false and handoff still skips.
challenge.resolution: Require exact equality for both provenance and showroomEvidence in one regression.

challenge.scenario: Only selected showroom fields are forwarded.
challenge.finding: Navigation completeness can fail later despite a nominal non-empty showroom array.
challenge.resolution: Forward the exact report array and deep-equality test the full rows.

challenge.finding: The quality API becomes a second provenance owner and can disagree with compiler output.
challenge.resolution: Only assign build.report.provenance; no reconstruction helper is permitted.

challenge.scenario: Regression reads source text but not runtime JSON.
challenge.finding: Serialization or response shaping could still drop the fields.
challenge.resolution: Invoke the real GET handler under VISUAL_FIDELITY_QA=1 and inspect returned JSON.

challenge.scenario: The fix accidentally changes accepted/quality-candidate records.
challenge.resolution: Modify only the factoryCandidates object and assert existing top-level contract remains unchanged.

challenge.scenario: A compiler-blocked recipe is forced into the catalog to satisfy the test.
challenge.finding: Product Owner readiness semantics would be weakened.
challenge.resolution: Retain the existing productOwnerReady exclusion branch unchanged.

challenge.scenario: Handoff readiness predicates are relaxed after propagation.
challenge.finding: The target could become reachable without real identity/showroom proof.
challenge.resolution: No change is allowed in Product Owner readiness predicates for this transaction.

challenge.scenario: The data flow works for Loot Vault only through hard-coded values.
challenge.finding: The generic Factory pipeline remains broken for later recipes.
challenge.resolution: Forward fields generically for every build.report rather than naming a template.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on this plan-only commit before editing runtime code.
Invoke the real visual-fidelity catalog GET handler with VISUAL_FIDELITY_QA enabled and locate gaming.loot-vault v2 factoryCandidate.
Deep-compare catalog provenance and showroomEvidence against buildRegisteredStorefrontTemplateFactoryCandidate().report.
Assert the existing quality-gate and handoff scripts still require factoryIdentityPinned and showroomContractPassed rather than bypassing them.
Run exact-head Quality Tests, TypeScript, Production Build, Completion Truth and CLOSE→LEARN lifecycle.

requirements.requirement: The Factory quality catalog propagates compiler-owned provenance and showroomEvidence unchanged for every Product Owner-ready factory candidate.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Factory provenance or showroom evidence may not disappear or be reconstructed at the catalog boundary.

requirements.requirement: Existing Product Owner readiness continues to require factory identity and showroom contract proof, and the repaired catalog now supplies the evidence those predicates consume.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No readiness predicate may be removed or bypassed to make the handoff reachable.

requirements.requirement: The exact implementation head typechecks and production-builds with the repaired catalog contract.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The evidence-flow repair must not introduce TypeScript or production build regressions.

notes: Targeted handoff dataflow repair only. Golden visual sensitivity and shipping/payment are separate release-budget transactions. No handoff predicate weakening, no compiler redesign, no parallel quality authority. Plan projection reconciled to exact canonical scope: storefront-ui included, projected failure/negative knowledge sets pinned, and specialist roles normalized to the canonical role set.
